page.layout: One column of running text, with the page number and running head at the top. The right margin holds only a library stamp, which is not transcribed. The catchword "armis" stands at the lower right below the last line.

main_text.p: turna & atrox pugna, nec certamen remissius, quam si pro summo honore ac gloriâ gentis utriusque ageretur. Incrudescente vero prælio, forte agminum duces invicem occurrunt, ferroque ita inter se concurrunt, ut libenter publi-cum bellum, in singulare certamen commutarent, quo Victoria[?] paucorum sanguine, imo vel alterutrius ducis, toti exercitui parta foret. Signo itaque regressus dato, uterque exercitus à pugnâ cessavit. Describitur circus, descendunt in certamen exercituum præfecti, paribus armis & animis. Lex singulari congressui adjicitur, ut si Frontinus vincat, libera sit à Suenonibus Dania; si victoriam reportaverit Attilus, Dania Suecis tributum pendat, & se victam fateatur. Quo evenit, ut crebrescentibus utrinque vulneribus, Attilus armis

page.notes: The first word "turna" is a fragment of a word from the previous page and is kept as a fragment. "Victoria" is partly covered by the library stamp in the right margin, so the opening letters are marked [?]. Long s is rendered as s throughout. The printed f in "fi", "fine" and similar words is read as long s. Some hyphenated line ends are uncertain and may be read differently from the printed hyphens.
